chunks: Saad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Dharih ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Prayer of Ja'far, to be counted from my voluntary prayers, so he said: 'Whatever you wish, from night or day.'

From him, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, who said: I wrote to the Last One (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who prayed the Prayer of Ja'far for two rak'ahs, then was hastened away from the last two rak'ahs by a need, or interrupted that by an incident; is it permissible for him to complete them when he finishes from his need, and if he stands from his place? Or does he not count that unless he restarts the prayer and prays all four rak'ahs in one place? So he wrote: 'Yes, if something unavoidable interrupts him from that, let him interrupt that, then let him return and build upon what remained of it, if God Almighty wills.'

key_terms.الْمَاضِي الْآخِرُ: The Last One (a title for Imam al-Hadi or Imam al-Hasan al-Askari)
key_terms.صَلَاةُ جَعْفَرٍ: Prayer of Ja'far (a specific voluntary prayer)

ai.seo_question: How to complete Salat al-Ja'far if interrupted by a necessary need?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of Salat al-Ja'far, a four-rak'ah voluntary prayer, by confirming its permissibility at any time, day or night. It further establishes the jurisprudential principle of *ibtida'* (resuming) rather than *i'dad* (restarting) when interrupted by an unavoidable necessity, allowing the worshipper to complete the remaining rak'ahs in the same sitting.
